questions.stem: Find the exact Simple Interest (SI) earned on a principal amount of Rs. 1000 for a duration of 2 years at an interest rate of 10% per annum.
questions.explanation: The formula for Simple Interest is SI = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100. Substituting the given values: SI = (1000 × 10 × 2) / 100 = 20000 / 100 = Rs. 200.

questions.stem: What is the exact Compound Interest (CI) earned on Rs. 1000 for 2 years at 10% per annum, if the interest is compounded annually?
The absolute mathematical difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a certain sum of money for exactly 2 years at 5% per annum is Rs. 15. Find the original sum.
questions.explanation: For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by the formula: Diff = P(R/100)². So, 15 = P(5/100)² = P(1/20)² = P(1/400). Multiplying both sides by 400 gives P = 15 × 400 = Rs. 6000.

questions.stem: A sum of money smoothly amounts to exactly Rs. 5200 in 5 years and exactly Rs. 5680 in 7 years strictly at simple interest. What is the precise rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: SI for 2 years (from year 5 to year 7) = 5680 - 5200 = Rs. 480. SI for 1 year = 480 / 2 = Rs. 240. SI for 5 years = 240 × 5 = Rs. 1200. Principal = Amount after 5 years - SI for 5 years = 5200 - 1200 = Rs. 4000. Rate = (100 × SI for 1 year) / (Principal × 1) = (100 × 240) / (4000) = 24000 / 4000 = 6%.

questions.stem: A specific sum of money placed securely at compound interest completely doubles itself in exactly 4 years. In how many total years will it amount to exactly eight times itself?
questions.explanation: In compound interest, if a sum becomes x times in T years, it will become x^n times in (n × T) years. Here, the sum becomes 2 times in 4 years. We want it to become 8 times, which is 2³. Here, x=2 and n=3. Required time = n × T = 3 × 4 = 12 years.

questions.stem: The accumulated compound interest on a certain sum for exactly 2 years is Rs. 410, whereas the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate is Rs. 400. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: SI for 2 years is Rs. 400, so SI for 1 year is Rs. 200. The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is 410 - 400 = Rs. 10. In CI, this extra Rs. 10 is the interest earned in the second year strictly on the interest of the first year (which was Rs. 200). Rate = (10 / 200) × 100 = 5%.

questions.stem: A total sum of Rs. 2600 is divided between A and B such that the simple interest on A's part at 10% for 5 years is exactly equal to the simple interest on B's part at 9% for 6 years. Find the exact amount given to A.
questions.explanation: Let A's share be A and B's share be B. A × 10 × 5 / 100 = B × 9 × 6 / 100. So, 50A = 54B. Simplifying the ratio, A/B = 54/50 = 27/25. The total ratio parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts. 52 parts = Rs. 2600. 1 part = 2600 / 52 = Rs. 50. A's share = 27 parts = 27 × 50 = Rs. 1350.
